text:
In no man's land, on the dust

trodden by those who go and those who come,

I have pitched my tent without shelter

and I watch whether they go or return.

Some say I am among those who go,

although I am resting from the road.

Others "know" that I return, although I keep silent;

and my truest route I do not tell.

I tried to prove that where I am going

is to myself, only to myself, to have myself.

And they smile on hearing it, because all of them

are people who go, but who return.

Listen to me once: I no longer care

about the roads here, worth so much.

Because I walked once, I have already stopped

to root myself in the land that is no one's.

translation.title: In No Man's Land
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the road paradox and the decision to root in no one's land.
